components.note: A single-leaf door swinging on its hinge; the simplified form keeps the idea of a door, later extended to the household behind it.

example.hanzi: 这个小区住着两百多户人家。
example.pinyin: Zhège xiǎoqū zhù zhe liǎng bǎi duō hù rénjiā.
example.english: Over two hundred households live in this neighborhood.
example.fact: 户 counts households (一户人家) and builds 窗户 (window), 账户 (account) and 户口, the household registration system that ties residence to a place. Don't confuse 户 with 门, which is the general word for 'door'.

components.note: The parts of 幸 (土 over 丷 and 干) do not show a clear picture; treat it as a single unit.

example.pinyin: Xìnghǎo nǐ jíshí gǎndào le.
example.english: Luckily you arrived in time.
example.fact: 幸 gives 幸好 and 幸亏 ('fortunately'), 幸福 (happiness) and 不幸 (unfortunate). In a polite formal greeting, 幸会 is 'pleased to meet you', a phrase heard at business introductions.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — speaking, asking
寸 (hand/measure) — a hand reaching for something

example.pinyin: Wǒ tǎoyàn xià yǔ tiān.
example.english: I hate rainy days.
example.fact: 讨 literally 'to ask for' underlies 讨论 (discuss), 讨价还价 (haggle), 讨饭 (beg) and 讨厌, 'to dislike', literally 'to invite disgust'. 讨人喜欢 describes someone who is easy to like.

components.note: 见 (see) — the meaning side: looking
礻 (the form of 示, shì) gives the sound — it matches 视 exactly

example.pinyin: Wǒmen měitiān wǎnshang kàn diànshì.
example.english: We watch TV every evening.
example.fact: 视 is a formal 'to look' that lives in compounds: 电视 (TV), 视频 (video), 近视 (nearsighted), 重视 (to take seriously), 忽视 (to overlook). Spoken Chinese uses 看 for the plain act of looking.

components.note: 页 (head) — the 'head' of a text is its title
是 (shì) gives a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Zhè dào tí hěn nán.
example.english: This question is very hard.
example.fact: 题 counts test questions with 道: 一道题. It forms 问题 (question, problem — 没问题 means 'no problem'), 题目 (title or question) and 主题 (theme). In casual use 题 can sound like a quiz item.

components.note: 犭 (dog/beast) — fierce animals
孟 (mèng) gives the sound — only the tone differs

example.pinyin: Tā měng de tuīkāi le mén.
example.english: He suddenly pushed the door open.
example.fact: 猛 can mean 'fierce' (猛兽 wild beast, 凶猛) or 'suddenly and forcefully', as in 猛地 and 猛增 ('to soar'). A fierce attack is 猛烈, and 猛 + verb adds the idea of vigour.

components.note: 阝 (a mound or steps) — the original sense of steps being cleared
余 (yú) — surplus, also hinting at the sound

example.pinyin: Chúle nǐ, dàjiā dōu lái le.
example.english: Everyone came except you.
example.fact: 除 is a common word in 除了……以外 ('besides, except'). It also means 'divide' in math (除法, 6除以2 is 6 divided by 2) and gives 除夕 (New Year's Eve), the night that 'removes' the old year.

components.note: 雨 (rain) — drops falling scattered
令 (lìng) gives the sound — only the tone differs

example.hanzi: 今天早上的气温是零度。
example.pinyin: Jīntiān zǎoshang de qìwēn shì líng dù.
example.english: This morning's temperature is zero degrees.
example.fact: 零 is zero (not the older 〇, though both are used), and it also fills gaps in numbers: 一百零五 is 105, and 三千零二十 is 3,020. It also means 'odd, scattered', as in 零钱 (small change) and 零食 (snacks).

components.note: 日 (sun) — brightness and flashing light
光 (guāng) gives a rough sound clue to the character

example.pinyin: Chuán zài shuǐ shàng huàng lái huàng qù.
example.english: The boat sways back and forth on the water.
example.fact: 晃 has two readings: huàng means 'to shake, sway' (摇晃, 晃动), while huǎng means 'to dazzle' or 'flash past', as in 一晃 ('in a flash') and 晃眼. 晃来晃去 is a pattern, 'swaying back and forth'.

components.note: 又 (hand) — the lower part, a hand stretching something long

example.pinyin: Tā de wǔzī shífēn mànmiào.
example.english: Her dance movements are very graceful.
example.fact: 曼 is rarely used alone; it appears in 曼妙 (graceful, of a figure or dancing) and in transliterations such as 曼谷 (Bangkok), 曼哈顿 (Manhattan) and 曼联 (Manchester United).

excludeSuggestion: Bound character: it mainly occurs in 曼妙 and transliterated place names.

components.note: 氵 (water) — liquid dye
木 (wood/plants) — dyes were made from plants

example.pinyin: Tā bǎ tóufa rǎn chéng le zōngsè.
example.english: She dyed her hair brown.
example.fact: 染 means to dye or to colour (染发), and also to be infected or tainted: 感染 (infect), 传染 (spread, be contagious) and 污染 (pollute).

components.note: 氵 (water) — getting wet or stained by liquid
占 (zhàn) gives the sound — close to zhān

example.pinyin: Tā de shǒu shàng zhān le yìdiǎn yóu.
example.english: He got a bit of oil on his hand.
example.fact: 沾 describes getting a bit of something on you: 沾上 (to get stained). It also has figurative uses: 沾光 means to benefit from someone else's good fortune, and 沾边 means 'to be related to'.

components.note: 衤 (clothes) — a garment
库 (kù) gives the sound — it matches 裤 exactly

example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo kùzi tài cháng le.
example.english: These trousers are too long.
example.fact: 裤 is nearly always 裤子, and its measure word is 条 (一条裤子), because pants are viewed as long strips. 牛仔裤 (jeans) and 短裤 (shorts) are common, and 裤脚 is the hem of the trouser leg.

components.note: 礻 (altar/spirit) — blessings from the gods
畐 (fú) gives the sound — it matches 福 exactly

example.hanzi: 祝你新年幸福平安，福气满满。
example.pinyin: Zhù nǐ xīnnián xìngfú píng'ān, fúqi mǎnmǎn.
example.english: Wishing you happiness and peace in the new year, full of good fortune.
example.fact: At Chinese New Year 福 is pasted on doors, often upside down: 倒 (dào, 'upside down') sounds like 到 (dào, 'arrive'), so a 倒福 means 'fortune has arrived'. 福气 means 'good luck' or 'blessing'.

components.note: 罒 (net) — a legal charge or accusation
刂 (knife) — punishment by blade

example.hanzi: 他因为迟到被罚了一百元。
example.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi chídào bèi fá le yìbǎi yuán.
example.english: He was fined a hundred yuan for being late.
example.fact: 罚 means to punish and in daily life most often 'to fine': 罚款 (fine), 罚站 (make someone stand as punishment) and 处罚. 罚 is also in the pair 赏罚, 'reward and punishment'.

components.note: 方 (flag) — a banner leading a group
氏 — part of the old combined shape, giving a hint of 'a group of followers'

example.hanzi: 我们计划一次长途旅行。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen jìhuà yí cì chángtú lǚxíng.
example.english: We are planning a long trip.
example.fact: 旅 once denoted a military unit of five hundred soldiers, which is why 旅 can still translate as 'brigade'. It later widened to a group on the move: 旅行 (travel), 旅游 (tourism), 旅馆 (hotel) and 旅客 (traveler).

components.note: 厂 (building) — a covered structure
豆 (dòu) gives a loose sound hint to chú

example.pinyin: Māma zài chúfáng zuòfàn.
example.english: Mom is cooking in the kitchen.
example.fact: 厨 is a bound form found in 厨房 (kitchen), 厨师 (chef) and 下厨 ('to go into the kitchen', i.e. to cook). 厨 is the simplified form of 廚.

components.note: 彳 (step) — walking
夂 (a foot dragging) — coming behind another step

example.pinyin: Chī wán fàn hòu, wǒmen qù sànbù.
example.english: After eating, we go for a walk.
example.fact: 後 is the traditional form; simplified writing merges it into 后, which also means 'queen' (皇后). In traditional text 後 is 'after, behind', and 之後 is 'afterwards'.

excludeSuggestion: Traditional-only form; the simplified deck character is 后.

components.note: An old picture of a nail seen from above, whose meaning later shifted to 'fourth' and 'small cube'.

example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ tǔdòu qiē chéng dīng.
example.english: Please dice the potatoes.
example.fact: 丁 is the fourth in the ten Heavenly Stems (甲乙丙丁), so it is used like 'D' in a ranking. In cooking it means diced pieces (肉丁, 土豆丁), and it is also a common surname.

components.note: 衤 (clothes) — being without clothes
果 (guǒ) gives the sound — close to luǒ

example.hanzi: 他赤裸着上身在海边跑步。
example.pinyin: Tā chìluǒ zhe shàngshēn zài hǎibiān pǎobù.
example.english: He ran along the beach with his upper body bare.
example.fact: 裸 means 'bare', as in 裸露 and 裸眼 (naked eye, unaided vision). Modern Chinese has coined terms like 裸婚 ('naked wedding') for marrying without a house, car or ring.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — tearing by hand
斯 (sī) gives the sound — it matches 撕 exactly

example.hanzi: 他把那封信撕成了两半。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ nà fēng xìn sī chéng le liǎng bàn.
example.english: He tore the letter in two.
example.fact: 撕 describes tearing or ripping with the hands (撕开, 撕掉), while 扯 is 'to pull or yank'. In online slang, 撕 also means a public spat, so 撕起来了 is 'they've started a fight'.

components.note: 木 (wood) — a stake made of wood
庄 (zhuāng) gives the sound — it matches 桩 exactly

example.pinyin: Zhè shì yì zhuāng hěn zhòngyào de shì.
example.english: This is a very important matter.
example.fact: 桩 is a measure word for matters, cases and events: 一桩案子 (a case), 一桩心事 (something on one's mind). As a noun it is a stake or post — 打桩 (pile driving), and now 充电桩 (EV charging post).

components.note: 扌 (hand) — catching by hand
足 (zú) gives a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Māo zài zhuō lǎoshǔ.
example.english: The cat is catching mice.
example.fact: 捉 is a written-leaning verb for 'to catch', where spoken Chinese often prefers 抓. It appears in 捉迷藏 (hide-and-seek) and 捉弄 (to play a trick on someone), and 捉 can be used in 捉摸, 'to fathom'.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh) — an organ of the body
巿 (fú) gives a loose sound hint to fèi

example.pinyin: Xīyān duì fèi bù hǎo.
example.english: Smoking is bad for the lungs.
example.fact: 肺 is the lung, and it makes 肺炎 (pneumonia) and 肺活量 (lung capacity). The old pair 肺腑 (lungs and entrails) is a figure of speech for the heart: 肺腑之言 means words from the bottom of one's heart.

components.note: 阝 (a place or mound) — an enclosed area
完 (wán) gives a rough sound clue to yuàn

example.pinyin: Wǒ jiā yǒu yí gè xiǎo yuànzi.
example.english: My home has a small courtyard.
example.fact: 院 means a walled courtyard or compound and then an institution: 医院 (hospital), 学院 (college), 电影院 (cinema), 法院 (court). 住院 is 'to be hospitalized' and 院子 is the yard.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — one's own harvest, held privately
厶 — the old form of 私 itself, a sign of 'mine, private'

example.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ de sīrén diànhuà.
example.english: This is my private phone.
example.fact: 私 is the opposite of 公 (public): 私人 (private), 私立 (privately-run) and 私下 (in private) are common. 自私 means 'selfish', and 隐私 is 'privacy', the word at the heart of data-protection talk.

components.note: Its modern shape (龶 above 月) is a reduction of an older form, so the parts are not a dependable clue; learn it as a unit.

example.hanzi: 春天到了，山上一片青绿。
example.pinyin: Chūntiān dào le, shān shàng yí piàn qīnglǜ.
example.english: Spring has come and the mountains are fresh green.
example.fact: 青 covers a range from green to blue, even black: 青草 (green grass), 青天 (blue sky), 青丝 (black hair). It also means 'young', as in 青春 (youth) and 青年 (young people).

components.note: 木 (wood) — buckets were once made of wood
甬 (yǒng) gives a rough sound clue to tǒng

example.hanzi: 请把垃圾扔进垃圾桶里。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ lājī rēng jìn lājītǒng lǐ.
example.english: Please throw the garbage in the trash can.
example.fact: 桶 is a noun, and a measure word too: 一桶水 (a bucket of water). 水桶 is a bucket, 垃圾桶 is a trash can, and 桶装水 is 'bottled' (barrelled) water.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — counting out loud
十 (shí) gives a loose sound link to jì

example.pinyin: Wǒmen yǒu yí gè xīn de jìhuà.
example.english: We have a new plan.
example.fact: 计 is the base of many words: 计划 (plan), 计算 (calculate), 设计 (design), 统计 (statistics), 会计 (accountant). It can also be a 'ruse' in set phrases: 上了他的计 means 'fell for his trick'.

components.note: 酉 (wine jar) — a fermented food
丬 gives the sound here, a rough match to jiàng

example.hanzi: 我喜欢在面包上抹果酱。
example.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan zài miànbāo shàng mǒ guǒjiàng.
example.english: I like to spread jam on bread.
example.fact: 酱 covers thick fermented or pasty sauces: 酱油 (soy sauce), 豆瓣酱 (chili bean paste), 果酱 (jam) and 番茄酱 (ketchup). In internet slang 酱紫 imitates 这样子, 'like this'.

components.note: 力 (strength) — using force to take something
去 (qù) gives a loose sound hint to jié

example.pinyin: Yínháng bèi rén qiǎngjié le.
example.english: The bank was robbed.
example.fact: 劫 is the verb for robbing by force (抢劫, 劫持 'hijack'), and it also means 'calamity' via Buddhism (劫难, 'a catastrophe'), as in the idiom 在劫难逃 ('doomed to meet the fate').

components.note: 王 (jade) — rings were made of jade
不 (bù) in this simplified form replaces the complex part of 環 and is not a true sound clue

example.pinyin: Wǒmen yào bǎohù huánjìng.
example.english: We must protect the environment.
example.fact: 环 is the ring or loop in 耳环 (earring), 环境 (environment) and 环保 (environmental protection). In Beijing, ring roads are named 二环, 三环 and so on, and addresses are placed 'inside the third ring'.

components.note: An outline of a cliff overhang or shed roof; as a character it is also the simplified form of 廠, giving 'factory'.

example.pinyin: Tā zài yì jiā gōngchǎng gōngzuò.
example.english: He works in a factory.
example.fact: 厂 is the simplified writing of 廠 'factory' and forms 工厂, 厂长 (factory director) and 钢厂. The same shape is also the 'cliff' radical (read hǎn), which sits at the upper left of many characters.

components.note: 车 (cart) — a vehicle, the traditional meaning side; its link to 'soft' is historical
欠 (qiàn) gives a loose sound clue to ruǎn

example.pinyin: Zhè zhāng shāfā hěn ruǎn.
example.english: This sofa is very soft.
example.fact: 软 is the opposite of 硬, hence 软件 (software) vs 硬件 (hardware). It also describes weakness or leniency: 软弱 (weak), 心软 (soft-hearted), and 软卧 (soft sleeper) is a train class in China.

components.note: 角 (horn) — an animal butting with its horns
虫 (chóng) gives a loose sound clue to chù

example.hanzi: 别触碰那个红色的按钮。
example.pinyin: Bié chùpèng nàge hóngsè de ànniǔ.
example.english: Don't touch that red button.
example.fact: 触 originally pictured butting with horns and now means 'to touch': 接触 (contact), 触摸屏 (touchscreen), 触动 (to stir the heart). 触 is not a spoken word on its own; it usually appears in compounds.

components.note: A picture of a rodent, with teeth, whiskers and a tail; the modern form is much simplified.

example.pinyin: Māo zài zhuā lǎoshǔ.
example.english: The cat is catching a mouse.
example.fact: Chinese does not distinguish mouse from rat: 老鼠 covers both. 鼠 is the first animal in the zodiac, and 鼠标 ('mouse mark') is the computer mouse.

components.note: 阝 (mound) — a place or hill
东 (east) — a direction; in this simplified form it replaces part of the older 陳

example.pinyin: Chén lǎoshī jiāo wǒmen shùxué.
example.english: Teacher Chen teaches us math.
example.fact: 陈 is one of the most common surnames. As a word it means 'to arrange or display' (陈列) and 'old, stale' (陈旧, 陈醋 'aged vinegar').

components.note: 钅 (metal) — silver is a metal
艮 (gèn) gives a loose sound clue to yín

example.pinyin: Tā dàizhe yì tiáo yín xiàngliàn.
example.english: She is wearing a silver necklace.
example.fact: 银 is silver and, because silver was once the currency, it stands in money words: 银行 (bank, literally 'silver firm'), 银牌 (silver medal) and 银色 (silver color). 水银 is mercury, 'water-silver'.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — a steady harvest
㥯 (yǐn/wěn) gives the sound — a rare character

example.pinyin: Zhè zuò qiáo hěn wěn.
example.english: This bridge is very stable.
example.fact: 稳 is a common description of calm and reliability: 稳定 (stable), 稳重 (sedate), 稳妥 (safe). In slang, 稳了 means 'it's in the bag': 这次考试稳了 ('I'm sure to pass this test').

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — scrubbing with a cloth
刂 (blade) — a scraping motion

example.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān shuā yá liǎng cì.
example.english: I brush my teeth twice a day.
example.fact: 刷 covers all kinds of brushing: 刷牙 (brush teeth), 刷墙 (paint a wall), and 刷卡 (swipe a card). A modern sense is scrolling or repeating, as in 刷手机 ('scroll on one's phone').

components.note: 虍 (tiger stripes) — the head and stripes of a tiger
几 — the lower part of the shape, often read as the tiger's legs

example.hanzi: 动物园里有一只大老虎。
example.pinyin: Dòngwùyuán lǐ yǒu yì zhī dà lǎohǔ.
example.english: There is a big tiger in the zoo.
example.fact: 虎 usually appears as 老虎; it is a zodiac sign and a symbol of courage. 马虎 ('horse-tiger') is a funny word meaning careless, and 虎头蛇尾 describes starting strong and ending weakly.

components.note: 户 (door) — the top is a door
The lower part is a squashed form of 册 (a board with strips), as on a hung name-board.

example.pinyin: Lúntāi bèi zhā biǎn le.
example.english: The tire got punctured and went flat.
example.fact: 扁 means flat or squashed (扁平), and informally 'to beat someone up': 我要扁你! The same character is read piān in 扁舟 (a small boat) and biǎn can also describe a flat bean 扁豆.

components.note: 氵 (water) — a liquid
干 (gān) gives a rough sound clue to hàn

example.pinyin: Tā pǎo de mǎntóu dà hàn.
example.english: He ran until sweat was pouring from his head.
example.fact: 汗 is sweat: 出汗, 流汗, 冷汗 (cold sweat). 汗 is read hán in 可汗 (khan, a Mongolian ruler), so the same character can be a title; 汗颜 means 'to blush with shame'.

components.note: 心 (heart) — a feeling of understanding
如 (rú) gives a loose sound hint to shù

example.hanzi: 请恕我直言，这个计划有问题。
example.pinyin: Qǐng shù wǒ zhíyán, zhège jìhuà yǒu wèntí.
example.english: Forgive my bluntness, but this plan has problems.
example.fact: 恕 is the Confucian ideal of reciprocity and forgiveness: Confucius defined it as 'do not do to others what you would not want done to you'. It survives in 宽恕 (to forgive) and polite formulas like 恕我直言.

components.note: 酉 (wine jar) — aged wine going sour
夋 (qūn) also gives a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Zhège júzi tài suān le.
example.english: This tangerine is too sour.
example.fact: 酸 is sour, and also an aching sensation in muscles (腰酸, 腿酸 'my legs ache') and a feeling of sadness (心酸, 'heartache'). One of the five tastes, 酸甜苦辣咸 begins with 酸.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — supporting by hand
夫 (fū) gives the sound — it matches 扶 closely

example.pinyin: Tā fú zhe lǎorén guò mǎlù.
example.english: He helped the elderly man cross the road.
example.fact: 扶 means to steady someone with the hand (扶老人 'support an elderly person'), where 帮 is a general 'to help'. 扶手 is a handrail, and 扶贫 (poverty alleviation) is a policy term.

components.note: 门 (gate) — an entrance
马 (horse) — a horse charging through the gate

example.hanzi: 他闯红灯被警察拦住了。
example.pinyin: Tā chuǎng hóngdēng bèi jǐngchá lánzhù le.
example.english: He ran a red light and was stopped by the police.
example.fact: 闯 is to burst in without permission or to go out into the world: 闯红灯 (run a red light), 闯祸 (cause trouble), and 闯荡 ('to make one's way in the world'). 走南闯北 means to travel widely.

components.note: 土 (earth) — a raised platform or ground
尚 (shàng) gives a rough sound clue to táng

example.pinyin: Wǒmen zài shítáng chī wǔfàn.
example.english: We eat lunch in the canteen.
example.fact: 堂 names a large hall: 食堂 (canteen), 教堂 (church), 礼堂 (auditorium). It counts class periods (一堂课), and 堂哥 / 堂姐 are paternal cousins who share your surname.

components.note: 犭 (dog/beast) — fierce animals
艮 (gèn) gives a loose sound clue to hěn

example.pinyin: Tā de xīn zhēn hěn.
example.english: He is truly ruthless.
example.fact: 狠 is 'fierce, merciless', as in 狠心 (hard-hearted) and 狠狠地 (fiercely, hard). Learners often mix it up with 很 ('very'): 狠 has the dog radical and means fierce, while 很 is the common adverb.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — twisting by hand
丑 (chǒu) gives a loose sound clue to niǔ

example.hanzi: 他扭了一下脚，走不了路。
example.pinyin: Tā niǔ le yíxià jiǎo, zǒu bù liǎo lù.
example.english: He twisted his foot and can't walk.
example.fact: 扭 covers twisting and spraining: 扭头 (turn the head), 扭伤 (sprain), 扭曲 (distort). 扭秧歌 is a folk dance in north China, where dancers sway with a twisting step.
